definitionEn: To be very close to doing something.
example1: We are about to leave for the airport.
example1Es: Estamos a punto de salir hacia el aeropuerto.
example2: She was about to speak when he interrupted.
example2Es: Estaba a punto de hablar cuando él interrumpió.

definitionEn: To be someone's responsibility to decide, or to be doing something sneaky.
example1: It is up to you to make the final decision.
example1Es: Depende de ti tomar la decisión final.
example2: What are those kids up to in the backyard?
example2Es: ¿Qué están tramando esos niños en el patio trasero?

definitionEn: to be wearing a piece of clothing.
example1: What do you have on today?
example1Es: ¿Qué llevas puesto hoy?
example2: She had a red coat on.
example2Es: Llevaba puesto un abrigo rojo.

definitionEn: to receive something back that you previously had.
example1: Can I have my pen back, please?
example1Es: ¿Puedo recuperar mi bolígrafo, por favor?
example2: He finally had his book back after a month.
example2Es: Por fin recuperó su libro después de un mes.

definitionEn: to get rid of something or stop doing something
example1: The company decided to do away with paper forms.
example1Es: La empresa decidió deshacerse de los formularios de papel.
example2: Many traditions are hard to do away with.
example2Es: Muchas tradiciones son difíciles de eliminar.

definitionEn: to do something again because it was not done correctly the first time
example1: You made too many mistakes; you need to do this essay over.
example1Es: Cometiste demasiados errores; necesitas rehacer este ensayo.
example2: They had to do the kitchen over after the flood.
example2Es: Tuvieron que reformar la cocina después de la inundación.

definitionEn: To continue happening or doing something.
example1: What is going on outside?
example1Es: ¿Qué está pasando afuera?
example2: Please go on with your story.
example2Es: Por favor, continúa con tu historia.

definitionEn: To leave your house to go to a social event.
example1: We usually go out on Friday nights.
example1Es: Solemos salir los viernes por la noche.
example2: The sudden power surge caused all the streetlights to go out simultaneously.
example2Es: La repentina sobrecarga eléctrica provocó que todas las farolas se apagaran simultáneamente.

definitionEn: To examine or review something carefully.
example1: Let's go over the contract details once more.
example1Es: Repasemos los detalles del contrato una vez más.
example2: The audit committee will go over the financial statements before submitting them to the board.
example2Es: El comité de auditoría revisará minuciosamente los estados financieros antes de presentarlos a la junta.

meaningEs: estar al tanto de, saber acerca de
definitionEn: to have information or awareness concerning a particular topic or event
example1: Did you know about the changes in the schedule?
example1Es: ¿Estabas al tanto de los cambios en el horario?
example2: Few people know about this hidden restaurant.
example2Es: Poca gente sabe acerca de este restaurante escondido.

definitionEn: To rise from bed after sleeping.
example1: I usually get up at 7 AM every day.
example1Es: Normalmente me levanto a las 7 a.m. todos los días.
example2: The marathon runner struggled to get up after collapsing near the finish line.
example2Es: El maratonista luchó por levantarse tras desplomarse cerca de la línea de meta.

meaningEs: subirse a un medio de transporte
definitionEn: To board a bus, train, plane, or ship.
example1: Please get on the bus quickly.
example1Es: Por favor, suban al autobús rápido.
example2: Passengers must show a valid boarding pass before they can get on the aircraft.
example2Es: Los pasajeros deben mostrar una tarjeta de embarque válida antes de poder subir a la aeronave.

meaningEs: superar una enfermedad o un disgusto
definitionEn: To recover from an illness, shock, or difficult experience.
example1: It took her weeks to get over the flu.
example1Es: Le tomó semanas recuperarse de la gripe.
example2: It took the company several fiscal quarters to get over the loss of its key supplier.
example2Es: A la empresa le tomó varios trimestres fiscales recuperarse de la pérdida de su proveedor clave.

definitionEn: To have a harmonious relationship with someone.
example1: Do you get along with your coworkers?
example1Es: ¿Te llevas bien con tus compañeros de trabajo?
example2: The department heads must learn to get along if the merger is to succeed.
example2Es: Los jefes de departamento deben aprender a llevarse bien para que la fusión tenga éxito.

definitionEn: To consider a problem or decision carefully before making a choice.
example1: Let me think over your offer and I will reply tomorrow.
example1Es: Déjame pensarlo bien tu oferta y te responderé mañana.
example2: The candidate asked for forty-eight hours to think over the executive compensation package.
example2Es: El candidato pidió cuarenta y ocho horas para considerar detenidamente el paquete de compensación ejecutiva.

definitionEn: To invent or produce a new idea, excuse, or plan using your imagination.
example1: Who managed to think up such a brilliant solution?
example1Es: ¿Quién se las arregló para idear una solución tan brillante?
example2: The marketing team met to think up an innovative campaign for the product launch.
example2Es: El equipo de marketing se reunió para idear una campaña innovadora para el lanzamiento del producto.

definitionEn: To invent a story, excuse, or become friends again after an argument.
example1: He had to make up an excuse for being late.
example1Es: Tuvo que inventar una excusa por llegar tarde.
example2: They always argue, but they quickly make up.
example2Es: Siempre discuten, pero se reconcilian rápidamente.

definitionEn: To manage to see, hear, or understand someone or something with difficulty.
example1: I can't make out what the sign says in the distance.
example1Es: No alcanzo a distinguir lo que dice el letrero en la distancia.
example2: Through the dense morning fog, the captain could barely make out the outline of the harbor.
example2Es: A través de la densa niebla matutina, el capitán apenas pudo distinguir la silueta del puerto.

definitionEn: To steal something and hurry away with it.
example1: The thieves broke into the store and made off with the cash register.
example1Es: Los ladrones irrumpieron en la tienda y huyeron con la caja registradora.
example2: Cybercriminals breached the secure database and made off with thousands of encrypted records.
example2Es: Los ciberdelincuentes vulneraron la base de datos segura y huyeron con miles de registros cifrados.

meaningEs: despedir (a alguien en un aeropuerto, estación, etc.)
definitionEn: To go to an airport, station, etc., to say goodbye to someone leaving.
example1: We went to the station to see our friends off.
example1Es: Fuimos a la estación a despedir a nuestros amigos.
example2: She came to see me off at the airport.
example2Es: Ella vino a despedirme al aeropuerto.

meaningEs: ver a través de (no dejarse engañar)
definitionEn: To realize the truth about someone or something that is intended to deceive.
example1: I could see through his lies immediately.
example1Es: Pude calar sus mentiras de inmediato.
example2: She saw through his charming facade.
example2Es: Ella vio más allá de su fachada encantadora.

definitionEn: to leave the ground and begin to fly, or to remove clothing.
example1: The plane will take off in ten minutes.
example1Es: El avión despegará en diez minutos.
example2: Please take off your shoes before entering.
example2Es: Por favor, quítate los zapatos antes de entrar.

definitionEn: to keep someone or something safe and provided for, or to handle a task.
example1: Can you take care of my dog this weekend?
example1Es: ¿Puedes cuidar de mi perro este fin de semana?
example2: Don't worry about the reservation, I will take care of it.
example2Es: No te preocupes por la reserva, yo me encargaré de ello.

meaningEs: encontrarse con, tropezar con (algo/alguien por casualidad)
definitionEn: to find or meet by chance
example1: I came across an old photo while cleaning my room.
example1Es: Me encontré con una foto vieja mientras limpiaba mi habitación.
example2: She came across as very confident during the interview.
example2Es: Dio la impresión de ser muy segura de sí misma durante la entrevista.

meaningEs: idear, inventar, proponer (una idea o solución)
definitionEn: to produce or create an idea, plan, or answer
example1: We need to come up with a better marketing strategy.
example1Es: Necesitamos idear una mejor estrategia de marketing.
example2: Can you come up with a solution to this problem?
example2Es: ¿Puedes proponer una solución a este problema?

meaningEs: hacer ejercicio / resolver o salir bien
definitionEn: To engage in physical exercise or to happen or develop in a successful way.
example1: I like to work out at the gym three times a week.
example1Es: Me gusta hacer ejercicio en el gimnasio tres veces por semana.
example2: Don't worry about the problem; everything will work out in the end.
example2Es: No te preocupes por el problema; al final todo saldrá bien.

meaningEs: trabajar en / esforzarse en mejorar algo
definitionEn: To spend time and effort trying to repair, improve, or achieve something.
example1: She is working on a new design for the website.
example1Es: Ella está trabajando en un nuevo diseño para el sitio web.
example2: I need to work on my pronunciation.
example2Es: Necesito trabajar en mi pronunciación.

definitionEn: To consume or finish completely so that nothing is left.
example1: We used up all the milk, so we need to buy more.
example1Es: Nos gastamos toda la leche, así que necesitamos comprar más.
example2: He used up his energy running the marathon.
example2Es: Agotó sus energías corriendo la maratón.

definitionEn: To try to find someone or something.
example1: I am looking for my keys.
example1Es: Estoy buscando mis llaves.
example2: She spent the entire afternoon looking for her missing cat.
example2Es: Pasó toda la tarde buscando a su gato perdido.

definitionEn: To take care of someone or something.
example1: Can you look after my dog this weekend?
example1Es: ¿Puedes cuidar a mi perro este fin de semana?
example2: Neighbors often look after each other's homes while traveling.
example2Es: Los vecinos a menudo se cuidan las casas mutuamente mientras viajan.

meaningEs: tener ilusión por, esperar con ilusión
definitionEn: to feel pleased and excited about something that is going to happen.
example1: I look forward to seeing you soon.
example1Es: Espero verte pronto con ilusión.
example2: She is looking forward to her birthday party.
example2Es: Ella está deseando que llegue su fiesta de cumpleaños.

definitionEn: Used to warn someone to be careful.
example1: Look out! There is a car coming.
example1Es: ¡Cuidado! Viene un carro.
example2: You need to look out for sudden changes in the weather on the mountain.
example2Es: Debes estar atento a los cambios repentinos en el clima de la montaña.

definitionEn: To stop trying or to stop doing a regular habit or activity.
example1: Never give up on your dreams.
example1Es: Nunca te rindas en tus sueños.
example2: He decided to give up smoking for the sake of his health.
example2Es: Decidió dejar de fumar por el bien de su salud.

definitionEn: To give something as a gift without charging money, or to reveal hidden information.
example1: She decided to give away her old books to the local library.
example1Es: Decidió regalar sus libros viejos a la biblioteca local.
example2: Be careful not to give away the ending of the movie.
example2Es: Ten cuidado de no revelar el final de la película.

definitionEn: To return something to the person who gave it to you.
example1: Please give me back my pen when you finish writing.
example1Es: Por favor, devuélveme mi bolígrafo cuando termines de escribir.
example2: He promised to give back the borrowed money by next Friday.
example2Es: Prometió devolver el dinero prestado para el próximo viernes.

definitionEn: To finally agree to something after refusing, or to submit homework/documents.
example1: After hours of negotiation, the management finally gave in to the union demands.
example1Es: Después de horas de negociación, la gerencia finalmente cedió a las demandas del sindicato.
example2: All students must give in their essays by Friday morning.
example2Es: Todos los estudiantes deben entregar sus ensayos antes del viernes por la mañana.

definitionEn: to discover a fact or piece of information.
example1: I need to find out what time the train leaves.
example1Es: Necesito averiguar a qué hora sale el tren.
example2: Don't let them find out about the surprise party.
example2Es: No dejes que se enteren de la fiesta sorpresa.

meaningEs: ceder, dar su brazo a torcer
definitionEn: to stop demanding something or to admit that you are wrong
example1: Neither side was willing to back down during the negotiations.
example1Es: Ninguna de las partes estaba dispuesta a ceder durante las negociaciones.
example2: Facing intense public scrutiny, the senator was forced to back down on the controversial amendment.
example2Es: Ante el intenso escrutinio público, el senador se vio obligado a dar su brazo a torcer con la controvertida enmienda.

meaningEs: respaldar, hacer una copia de seguridad
definitionEn: to give support to someone or to make a digital copy of data
example1: Always back up your important files before updating the software.
example1Es: Haz siempre una copia de seguridad de tus archivos importantes antes de actualizar el software.
example2: Can you back me up in this meeting?
example2Es: ¿Puedes respaldarme en esta reunión?

definitionEn: to become smooth, equal, or balanced after a period of fluctuation
example1: Prices tend to fluctuate in summer, but they usually even out by autumn.
example1Es: Los precios tienden a fluctuar en verano, pero normalmente se nivelan hacia el otoño.
example2: Economists predict that supply and demand will even out once production capacity stabilizes.
example2Es: Los economistas predicen que la oferta y la demanda se nivelarán una vez que la capacidad de producción se estabilice.

definitionEn: To be able to distinguish between two very similar people or things.
example1: The puppies are so identical that I cannot tell them apart.
example1Es: Los cachorros son tan idénticos que no puedo distinguirlos.
example2: Can you tell apart the original painting from the copy?
example2Es: ¿Puedes diferenciar la pintura original de la copia?

definitionEn: To speak angrily to someone because they have done something wrong.
example1: The teacher told him off for arriving late to class.
example1Es: El profesor le regañó por llegar tarde a clase.
example2: She was told off by her boss for making a careless mistake.
example2Es: Su jefe la regañó por cometer un error por descuido.

definitionEn: To decide that a planned event or activity will not happen.
example1: They had to call off the football match because of heavy rain.
example1Es: Tuvieron que suspender el partido de fútbol debido a la fuerte lluvia.
example2: The strike was called off after successful negotiations.
example2Es: La huelga fue cancelada tras unas negociaciones exitosas.

definitionEn: To telephone someone again or return a phone call.
example1: She is busy right now; can you call back in an hour?
example1Es: Está ocupada ahora mismo; ¿puede volver a llamar en una hora?
example2: I will call him back as soon as I finish this report.
example2Es: Le devolveré la llamada tan pronto como termine este informe.

definitionEn: To require or demand something, or to go to a place to collect someone.
example1: This situation calls for immediate action from the authorities.
example1Es: Esta situación exige una acción inmediata por parte de las autoridades.
example2: I will call for you at eight o'clock so we can go together.
example2Es: Pasaré a buscarte a las ocho para que podamos ir juntos.

definitionEn: To arrive or appear at a place, often unexpectedly or late.
example1: He didn't show up for the meeting yesterday.
example1Es: No se presentó a la reunión de ayer.
example2: Many guests showed up late to the party.
example2Es: Muchos invitados llegaron tarde a la fiesta.

definitionEn: To behave in a way that is intended to attract attention or impress others.
example1: He loves to show off his new sports car.
example1Es: Le encanta presumir su nuevo coche deportivo.
example2: Stop showing off and just play the game normally.
example2Es: Deja de presumir y juega con normalidad.

meaningEs: hacer la transición / cambiar de sistema
definitionEn: To move from using one system, method, or product to another.
example1: The factory plans to change over to renewable energy next year.
example1Es: La fábrica planea cambiar a energía renovable el próximo año.
example2: We are ready to change over to the new software platform.
example2Es: Estamos listos para hacer la transición a la nueva plataforma de software.

definitionEn: To yearn for or strongly desire someone or something.
example1: He longs for the days when he lived by the ocean.
example1Es: Anhela los días en que vivía junto al mar.
example2: Exiled diplomats often long for the familiar landscapes and culture of their homeland.
example2Es: Los diplomáticos exiliados a menudo anhelan los paisajes y la cultura familiares de su tierra natal.

definitionEn: To have a desire for something or want to do something.
example1: I feel like eating pizza tonight.
example1Es: Tengo ganas de comer pizza esta noche.
example2: Do you feel like going out for a walk?
example2Es: ¿Te apetece salir a dar un paseo?

meaningEs: sentirse con ánimos o fuerzas para hacer algo
definitionEn: To have the energy and strength to do something.
example1: I don't really feel up to going to the party tonight.
example1Es: No me siento con muchos ánimos de ir a la fiesta esta noche.
example2: After recovering from surgery, she finally felt up to resuming her administrative duties.
example2Es: Tras recuperarse de la cirugía, por fin se sintió con fuerzas para reanudar sus tareas administrativas.

definitionEn: To record information on paper so that you do not forget it.
example1: Please write down the address before you forget it.
example1Es: Por favor anota la dirección antes de que la olvides.
example2: He wrote down everything the teacher said.
example2Es: Él anotó todo lo que dijo el profesor.

meaningEs: contestar por carta o correo electrónico
definitionEn: To reply to someone by writing a letter or email.
example1: Thank you for your email; I will write back soon.
example1Es: Gracias por tu correo electrónico; responderé pronto.
example2: She received the letter but didn't write back.
example2Es: Ella recibió la carta pero no contestó.

definitionEn: To put on an item of clothing to see if it fits and looks good.
example1: Can I try on these blue jeans, please?
example1Es: ¿Puedo probarme estos vaqueros azules, por favor?
example2: She tried the jacket on before buying it.
example2Es: Ella se probó la chaqueta antes de comprarla.

meaningEs: probar algo (equipo, sistema) para ver su funcionamiento
definitionEn: To test something such as a machine, system, or method to see how well it works.
example1: We want to try out the new software before purchasing the license.
example1Es: Queremos probar el nuevo software antes de comprar la licencia.
example2: He went to the track to try out his new bicycle.
example2Es: Él fue a la pista para probar su bicicleta nueva.

definitionEn: To not include someone or something.
example1: You accidentally left out one important detail in your report.
example1Es: Sin darte cuenta omitiste un detalle importante en tu informe.
example2: Make sure not to leave anyone out of the invitation list.
example2Es: Asegúrate de no excluir a nadie de la lista de invitaciones.

definitionEn: To leave a place or person without taking them with you, or to outpace someone.
example1: He hurried so much that he left his keys behind.
example1Es: Se dio tanta prisa que se dejó las llaves atrás.
example2: She decided to leave her hometown behind and move to London.
example2Es: Ella decidió dejar atrás su ciudad natal y mudarse a Londres.

definitionEn: To be counted as part of a group or category.
example1: I number him among my closest friends.
example1Es: Lo cuento entre mis amigos más cercanos.
example2: The university is proud to number several Nobel laureates among its distinguished faculty.
example2Es: La universidad se enorgullece de contar a varios premios Nobel entre su distinguido cuerpo docente.

definitionEn: To admit that you have done something wrong.
example1: He finally owned up to breaking the window.
example1Es: Finalmente confesó haber roto la ventana.
example2: The accountant decided to own up to the bookkeeping discrepancy before the external audit began.
example2Es: El contable decidió admitir la discrepancia en los libros antes de que comenzara la auditoría externa.

definitionEn: To give something to someone else, especially when you do not want to.
example1: She found it hard to part with her childhood toys.
example1Es: Le costó desprenderse de sus juguetes de infancia.
example2: The collector refused to part with the rare manuscript, regardless of how much money was offered.
example2Es: El coleccionista se negó a desprenderse del raro manuscrito, sin importar cuánto dinero le ofrecieran.

definitionEn: To draw attention to something or someone.
example1: The teacher pointed out a spelling mistake in my essay.
example1Es: El profesor señaló un error ortográfico en mi ensayo.
example2: The lead researcher pointed out that the experimental sample size was too limited to draw conclusions.
example2Es: El investigador principal señaló que el tamaño de la muestra experimental era demasiado limitado para sacar conclusiones.

meaningEs: echar una mano, ayudar en una situación difícil
definitionEn: to assist someone, especially by working for them or giving them money
example1: My brother offered to help me out with my moving process.
example1Es: Mi hermano se ofreció a echarme una mano con mi proceso de mudanza.
example2: We always try to help out when our neighbors are in trouble.
example2Es: Siempre intentamos ayudar cuando nuestros vecinos están en problemas.

definitionEn: to invite someone to go with you to a restaurant, cinema, etc., on a date
example1: He finally gathered the courage to ask her out.
example1Es: Finalmente reunió el valor para invitarla a salir.
example2: Mark wants to ask out his colleague from the marketing department.
example2Es: Mark quiere invitar a salir a su compañera del departamento de marketing.

definitionEn: to request to have or receive something
example1: You should ask for help if you are struggling with the report.
example1Es: Deberías pedir ayuda si estás batallando con el informe.
example2: The customer asked for the manager to lodge a formal complaint.
example2Es: El cliente pidió al gerente para presentar una queja formal.

meaningEs: poner en marcha, arrancar (un motor, empresa)
definitionEn: to begin operating or to cause a machine, system, or business to begin operating
example1: He used his savings to start up a tech company.
example1Es: Usó sus ahorros para poner en marcha una empresa tecnológica.
example2: The engine was cold and took a while to start up.
example2Es: El motor estaba frío y tardó un rato en arrancar.

definitionEn: to discuss a problem or situation thoroughly, especially before making a decision
example1: Let's talk over the contract details before signing.
example1Es: Vamos a debatir los detalles del contrato antes de firmar.
example2: She wanted to talk over her career options with a mentor.
example2Es: Ella quería analizar detalladamente sus opciones de carrera con un mentor.

meaningEs: responder de mal modo, contestar mal (a una autoridad)
definitionEn: to reply rudely to someone in authority
example1: Children should not talk back to their parents or teachers.
example1Es: Los niños no deben contestar mal a sus padres o maestros.
example2: When the supervisor scolded him, he knew better than to talk back.
example2Es: Cuando el supervisor lo regañó, fue lo suficientemente prudente como para no replicar.

definitionEn: To delay doing something until a later time.
example1: We had to put off the meeting until next week.
example1Es: Tuvimos que posponer la reunión hasta la próxima semana.
example2: Don't put it off any longer.
example2Es: No lo pospongas más tiempo.

definitionEn: To accept an unpleasant situation or person without complaining.
example1: I can't put up with this noise anymore.
example1Es: No puedo soportar este ruido más.
example2: She puts up with a lot of stress at work.
example2Es: Ella soporta mucho estrés en el trabajo.

definitionEn: To dress yourself in clothes or switch on a device.
example1: Put on your coat, it's cold outside.
example1Es: Ponte el abrigo, hace frío afuera.
example2: Could you put on the lights?
example2Es: ¿Podrías encender las luces?

meaningEs: terminar (haciendo algo o en algún lugar)
definitionEn: to finally be in a particular place or situation after a series of events.
example1: If you don't map your route, you might end up getting lost.
example1Es: Si no trazas tu ruta, podrías terminar perdiéndote.
example2: They ended up staying at the hotel because of the heavy rain.
example2Es: Terminaron hospedándose en el hotel debido a la fuerte lluvia.

meaningEs: subsistir de, vivir de (dinero/comida) o perdurar
definitionEn: To have enough money or food to survive, or to continue to exist.
example1: It is difficult to live on such a low salary nowadays.
example1Es: Es difícil vivir con un salario tan bajo hoy en día.
example2: The memories of our trip will live on forever.
example2Es: Los recuerdos de nuestro viaje perdurarán para siempre.

meaningEs: estar a la altura de, cumplir con las expectativas
definitionEn: To be as good as something or to reach the standard that was expected.
example1: The movie failed to live up to all the hype surrounding it.
example1Es: La película no estuvo a la altura de todo el revuelo que la rodeaba.
example2: He always tries to live up to his parents' high expectations.
example2Es: Él siempre intenta estar a la altura de las altas expectativas de sus padres.

definitionEn: To pretend to agree or cooperate with someone temporarily.
example1: I didn't believe his story, but I decided to play along.
example1Es: No creí su historia, pero decidí seguirle la corriente.
example2: Just play along with the prank until we reveal the surprise.
example2Es: Solo sigue la corriente con la broma hasta que revelemos la sorpresa.

definitionEn: To make something appear less important or serious than it really is.
example1: The politician tried to play down the severity of the economic crisis.
example1Es: El político intentó minimizar la gravedad de la crisis económica.
example2: She always plays down her own achievements.
example2Es: Ella siempre resta importancia a sus propios logros.

definitionEn: To happen or develop in a particular way over time.
example1: We need to wait and see how the situation will play out.
example1Es: Tenemos que esperar y ver cómo se desarrolla la situación.
example2: The drama played out on national television.
example2Es: El drama se desarrolló en la televisión nacional.

meaningEs: llenarse por completo (un hotel, evento, etc.)
definitionEn: to reserve all available rooms, seats, or tickets so that none are left.
example1: The best hotels in the city book up months before the festival.
example1Es: Los mejores hoteles de la ciudad se llenan con meses de anticipación al festival.
example2: Conference venues in the financial district tend to book up months in advance of the summit.
example2Es: Los recintos para conferencias en el distrito financiero suelen reservarse por completo con meses de antelación a la cumbre.

definitionEn: to check in or register at a hotel or event.
example1: We will book in as soon as we arrive at the resort.
example1Es: Nos registraremos en cuanto lleguemos al complejo turístico.
example2: International delegates must book in at the reception pavilion upon arriving at the convention center.
example2Es: Los delegados internacionales deben registrarse en el pabellón de recepción al llegar al centro de convenciones.

definitionEn: To disappoint someone by failing to do what you agreed to do.
example1: I promise I will not let you down.
example1Es: Prometo que no te decepcionaré.
example2: His poor performance let the team down.
example2Es: Su bajo rendimiento defraudó al equipo.

definitionEn: To allow someone or something to enter a place or room.
example1: Open the door and let the cat in.
example1Es: Abre la puerta y deja entrar al gato.
example2: Can you let me in, I forgot my keys?
example2Es: ¿Puedes dejarme entrar, olvidé mis llaves?

definitionEn: To release your grip on something or stop holding it.
example1: Hold on tight and do not let go.
example1Es: Agárrate fuerte y no te sueltes.
example2: It is time to let go of the past.
example2Es: Es hora de dejar ir el pasado.

definitionEn: To continue doing an action persistently.
example1: If you keep on practicing, you will improve.
example1Es: Si sigues practicando, mejorarás.
example2: He didn't listen to the warning and kept on driving.
example2Es: Él no escuchó la advertencia y siguió conduciendo.

meaningEs: mantener el ritmo, estar al día
definitionEn: To move or progress at the same rate as someone or something else.
example1: Walk slower! I can't keep up with you.
example1Es: ¡Camina más despacio! No puedo seguir tu ritmo.
example2: It is important to keep up with the latest technological changes.
example2Es: Es importante estar al día con los últimos cambios tecnológicos.

definitionEn: To arrange, organize, or build something so that it is ready for use.
example1: Can you help me set up my new computer?
example1Es: ¿Me puedes ayudar a configurar mi computadora nueva?
example2: They decided to set up a new business in town.
example2Es: Decidieron montar un nuevo negocio en la ciudad.

definitionEn: To start a journey.
example1: We need to set off early tomorrow morning.
example1Es: Necesitamos partir temprano mañana por la mañana.
example2: A sudden drop in stock prices set off a wave of panic selling across global exchanges.
example2Es: Una caída repentina en los precios de las acciones desató una ola de ventas por pánico en las bolsas globales.

definitionEn: To delay the progress of something, or to cost someone a particular amount of money.
example1: The bad weather set the construction work back by two weeks.
example1Es: El mal tiempo retrasó los trabajos de construcción dos semanas.
example2: That new car must have set him back a fortune.
example2Es: Ese coche nuevo debió haberle costado una fortuna.

definitionEn: To take further action in order to make sure that something is successful or to gather more information.
example1: I will follow up on this matter tomorrow morning.
example1Es: Daré seguimiento a este asunto mañana por la mañana.
example2: The company sent an email to follow up with the customers.
example2Es: La empresa envió un correo electrónico para dar seguimiento a los clientes.

definitionEn: To continue an action or task until it is completed.
example1: You started the project, now you must follow through.
example1Es: Empezaste el proyecto, ahora debes llevarlo hasta el final.
example2: The chief executive praised the engineering department for their ability to follow through on complex commitments.
example2Es: El director ejecutivo elogió al departamento de ingeniería por su capacidad para llevar a término compromisos complejos.

definitionEn: To use up or finish a supply of something.
example1: We are going to run out of milk soon.
example1Es: Nos vamos a quedar sin leche pronto.
example2: They ran out of money during their trip.
example2Es: Se quedaron sin dinero durante su viaje.

definitionEn: To meet someone unexpectedly.
example1: I ran into an old school friend at the supermarket.
example1Es: Me encontré con un viejo amigo de la escuela en el supermercado.
example2: The development team did not anticipate that they would run into major regulatory hurdles in the European market.
example2Es: El equipo de desarrollo no anticipó que se toparía con importantes obstáculos regulatorios en el mercado europeo.

definitionEn: to refuse an offer or request, or to reduce the volume or heat of a device
example1: He had to turn down the job offer because the salary was too low.
example1Es: Tuvo que rechazar la oferta de trabajo porque el salario era muy bajo.
example2: Please turn down the music, it is too loud.
example2Es: Por favor, baja la música, está muy alta.

definitionEn: to arrive or appear somewhere, often unexpectedly, or to increase the volume
example1: She suddenly turned up at the party without an invitation.
example1Es: Apareció de repente en la fiesta sin invitación.
example2: Can you turn up the heating? I am freezing.
example2Es: Puedes subir la calefacción? Me estoy congelando.

definitionEn: to stop a machine, light, or water supply by pressing a switch or turning a tap
example1: Don't forget to turn off the lights before leaving the office.
example1Es: No olvides apagar las luces antes de salir de la oficina.
example2: Laboratory protocols require technicians to turn off the ventilation system before sterilizing the chamber.
example2Es: Los protocolos de laboratorio exigen que los técnicos apaguen el sistema de ventilación antes de esterilizar la cámara.

definitionEn: to become something different or to transform into another thing or person
example1: The caterpillar will eventually turn into a butterfly.
example1Es: La oruga eventualmente se convertirá en mariposa.
example2: What started as an informal workshop soon turned into an influential annual industry conference.
example2Es: Lo que comenzó como un taller informal pronto se transformó en una influyente conferencia anual de la industria.

meaningEs: mencionar un tema / criar a un hijo
definitionEn: to start talking about a subject, or to take care of and raise a child
example1: Why did you have to bring up that embarrassing topic during dinner?
example1Es: ¿Por qué tuviste que sacar ese tema embarazoso durante la cena?
example2: She was born in London, but brought up in Scotland.
example2Es: Nació en Londres, pero se crió en Escocia.

definitionEn: to cause something to happen or make something occur
example1: The new technological revolution has brought about massive changes in communication.
example1Es: La nueva revolución tecnológica ha provocado cambios masivos en la comunicación.
example2: Technological disruption has brought about substantial restructuring in modern retail banking.
example2Es: La disrupción tecnológica ha provocado una reestructuración sustancial en la banca minorista moderna.

definitionEn: to return something to a place, or to cause someone to remember or feel something from the past
example1: That old song always brings back wonderful childhood memories.
example1Es: Esa vieja canción siempre trae de vuelta maravillosos recuerdos de la infancia.
example2: The museum launched an international petition to bring back historical artifacts taken during the colonial era.
example2Es: El museo lanzó una petición internacional para restituir artefactos históricos sustraídos durante la época colonial.

definitionEn: To give things to a group of people.
example1: The teacher will hand out the exam papers now.
example1Es: El profesor repartirá los exámenes ahora.
example2: Volunteers hand out food to the homeless every Sunday.
example2Es: Los voluntarios reparten comida a las personas sin hogar todos los domingos.

definitionEn: To submit homework, an assignment, or a document to an authority.
example1: Students must hand in their essays by Friday.
example1Es: Los estudiantes deben entregar sus ensayos antes del viernes.
example2: Did you hand in your application form on time?
example2Es: ¿Entregaste tu formulario de solicitud a tiempo?

definitionEn: To give responsibility or control of something to someone else.
example1: The criminal was forced to hand over his weapon.
example1Es: El criminal fue obligado a entregar su arma.
example2: The retiring CEO will hand over power to his successor next month.
example2Es: El director ejecutivo que se jubila entregará el poder a su sucesor el próximo mes.

definitionEn: To leave a place or start discussing/doing something new.
example1: It is time to forget the past and move on.
example1Es: Es hora de olvidar el pasado y seguir adelante.
example2: Let us move on to the next item on the agenda.
example2Es: Pasemos al siguiente punto de la agenda.

meaningEs: mudarse (a una casa), entrar a vivir
definitionEn: To start living in a new home.
example1: We are going to move in next weekend.
example1Es: Nos vamos a mudar el próximo fin de semana.
example2: The new tenants moved in yesterday.
example2Es: Los nuevos inquilinos se mudaron ayer.

definitionEn: To permanently leave your home or apartment.
example1: He had to move out when his lease expired.
example1Es: Tuvo que mudarse cuando expiró su contrato de alquiler.
example2: My roommate is moving out at the end of the month.
example2Es: Mi compañero de piso se muda a finales de mes.

meaningEs: nombrar en honor a, poner el nombre de alguien
definitionEn: To give someone or something the same name as another person or thing.
example1: He was named after his uncle.
example1Es: Le pusieron su nombre en honor a su tío.
example2: The newly discovered asteroid was named after the pioneering astrophysicist who mapped its trajectory.
example2Es: El asteroide recién descubierto fue nombrado en honor a la astrofísica pionera que trazó su trayectoria.

meaningEs: leer de principio a fin para revisar
definitionEn: To read something carefully from beginning to end to check for mistakes.
example1: Please read over your essay before submitting it.
example1Es: Por favor, lee tu ensayo antes de entregarlo.
example2: Before signing the acquisition agreement, our legal counsel will read over every single clause.
example2Es: Antes de firmar el acuerdo de adquisición, nuestro asesor jurídico leerá con detenimiento cada una de las cláusulas.

definitionEn: To read a lot about a subject in order to learn about it.
example1: I need to read up on the history of the company before the interview.
example1Es: Necesito informarme leyendo sobre la historia de la empresa antes de la entrevista.
example2: The young diplomat spent the weekend reading up on maritime law before attending the multilateral negotiations.
example2Es: El joven diplomático pasó el fin de semana documentándose sobre derecho marítimo antes de asistir a las negociaciones multilaterales.

meaningEs: abrir (un negocio/lugar), hablar con franqueza o crear oportunidades
definitionEn: To become open for business or to talk more freely about your feelings.
example1: A new coffee shop just opened up down the street.
example1Es: Una nueva cafetería acaba de abrir a la vuelta de la esquina.
example2: It took him a long time to open up about his past.
example2Es: Le tomó mucho tiempo abrirse sobre su pasado.

meaningEs: mandar a alguien, dar órdenes de forma autoritaria
definitionEn: To tell someone what to do all the time in an annoying way.
example1: He hates being ordered about by his older brother.
example1Es: Odia que su hermano mayor lo mande todo el tiempo.
example2: A competent manager inspires collaboration rather than attempting to order subordinates about.
example2Es: Un gerente competente inspira colaboración en lugar de intentar mangonear a sus subordinados.

definitionEn: To return money borrowed from someone, or to punish someone for treating you badly.
example1: I will pay you back tomorrow.
example1Es: Te devolveré el dinero mañana.
example2: He promised to pay back the loan within a year.
example2Es: Prometió devolver el préstamo en el plazo de un año.

definitionEn: To finish paying money owed for something, or to yield good results.
example1: She worked hard to pay off her student debt.
example1Es: Trabajó duro para saldar su deuda estudiantil.
example2: All his hard work finally paid off when he got the promotion.
example2Es: Todo su esfuerzo finalmente dio sus frutos cuando consiguió el ascenso.

definitionEn: to increase in amount, intensity, or size over a period of time.
example1: Stress can build up if you do not take breaks.
example1Es: El estrés puede acumularse si no tomas descansos.
example2: He is trying to build up his stamina by running every morning.
example2Es: Está intentando aumentar su resistencia corriendo todas las mañanas.

definitionEn: to use success or a previous achievement as a base for further progress.
example1: We need to build on our previous success to grow the business.
example1Es: Necesitamos basarnos en nuestro éxito anterior para hacer crecer el negocio.
example2: Our revised curriculum aims to build on the foundational analytical skills established in primary education.
example2Es: Nuestro plan de estudios revisado busca consolidar y ampliar las habilidades analíticas fundamentales adquiridas en la educación primaria.

definitionEn: to wait for a short time; to hold tightly onto something.
example1: Hold on a minute, I am almost ready.
example1Es: Espera un minuto, casi estoy listo.
example2: Hold on to the handrail so you do not fall.
example2Es: Agárrate fuerte al pasamanos para que no te caigas.

definitionEn: to stop yourself from showing emotion or moving forward.
example1: She tried to hold back her tears during the sad movie.
example1Es: Intentó contener sus lágrimas durante la película triste.
example2: Severe supply chain bottlenecks continue to hold back the expansion of domestic automobile manufacturing.
example2Es: Los severos cuellos de botella en la cadena de suministro continúan frenando la expansión de la fabricación nacional de automóviles.

definitionEn: To cause a particular outcome or to lead to something.
example1: Failure to plan can result in serious mistakes.
example1Es: No planificar puede resultar en errores graves.
example2: The accident resulted in heavy traffic delays.
example2Es: El accidente provocó grandes retrasos en el tráfico.

definitionEn: To occur as a consequence of something else.
example1: Most mistakes result from poor communication.
example1Es: La mayoría de los errores se deben a una mala comunicación.
example2: The confusion resulted from unclear instructions.
example2Es: La confusión se debió a instrucciones poco claras.

definitionEn: To find or meet someone or something by chance.
example1: While walking in the woods, they happened upon a hidden cabin.
example1Es: Mientras caminaban por el bosque, se encontraron por casualidad con una cabaña escondida.
example2: She happened upon an old diary in the attic.
example2Es: Se topó con un viejo diario en el ático por casualidad.

definitionEn: to stop operating permanently
example1: The factory had to close down due to bankruptcy.
example1Es: La fábrica tuvo que cerrar definitivamente debido a la bancarrota.
example2: They decided to close the store down after ten years.
example2Es: Decidieron cerrar la tienda definitivamente después de diez años.

definitionEn: to result in a specific consequence or event.
example1: Eating too much sugar can lead to health problems.
example1Es: Comer demasiado azúcar puede conducir a problemas de salud.
example2: What led to this unexpected decision?
example2Es: ¿Qué condujo a esta decisión inesperada?

meaningEs: comprar la parte a alguien, comprar una empresa
definitionEn: to pay someone for their share of a business or property.
example1: He decided to buy out his partners and run the company alone.
example1Es: Decidió comprar la parte de sus socios y dirigir la empresa solo.
example2: The multinational conglomerate offered a handsome premium to buy out the remaining minority shareholders.
example2Es: El conglomerado multinacional ofreció una atractiva prima para comprar la participación de los accionistas minoritarios restantes.

definitionEn: to buy all of something available.
example1: Investors began to buy up all the land near the coast.
example1Es: Los inversores empezaron a acaparar todas las tierras cerca de la costa.
example2: Speculative investment funds rushed to buy up prime commercial real estate along the newly constructed waterfront.
example2Es: Fondos de inversión especulativos se apresuraron a acaparar inmuebles comerciales de primer nivel a lo largo del paseo marítimo recién construido.

definitionEn: To accept and deal with an unpleasant fact or situation.
example1: It is time to face up to reality.
example1Es: Es hora de asumir la realidad.
example2: He refused to face up to his responsibilities.
example2Es: Se negó a asumir sus responsabilidades.

definitionEn: To spend all of one's money completely.
example1: He managed to spend out his savings during the trip.
example1Es: Se las arregló para gastar todos sus ahorros durante el viaje.
example2: To complete the municipal infrastructure upgrade, the local council had to spend out its reserve fund.
example2Es: Para completar la modernización de la infraestructura municipal, el ayuntamiento tuvo que desembolsar la totalidad de su fondo de reserva.

definitionEn: To move towards a specific place or goal.
example1: We need to head for the exit immediately.
example1Es: Necesitamos dirigirnos hacia la salida inmediatamente.
example2: They are heading for trouble if they continue like that.
example2Es: Se están metiendo en problemas si continúan así.

definitionEn: To return to a place where you were before.
example1: It is getting dark, so let's head back.
example1Es: Está oscureciendo, así que volvamos.
example2: As the blizzard intensified, mountaineers were instructed to abandon the summit attempt and head back to base camp.
example2Es: A medida que la ventisca se intensificaba, se instruyó a los montañistas abandonar el intento de cumbre y regresar al campamento base.

meaningEs: empollarse algo, estudiar a fondo un tema
definitionEn: to spend time reading and studying in order to learn about a particular subject
example1: I need to learn up on the new safety regulations before tomorrow's inspection.
example1Es: Necesito estudiar a fondo las nuevas normativas de seguridad antes de la inspección de mañana.
example2: She spent the weekend learning up the history of the region.
example2Es: Pasó el fin de semana empollándose la historia de la región.

definitionEn: to stop rising or falling and stay at a steady level
example1: House prices have finally begun to level off after years of rapid growth.
example1Es: Los precios de las viviendas finalmente han comenzado a estabilizarse tras años de rápido crecimiento.
example2: The aircraft climbed to ten thousand feet and then leveled off.
example2Es: El avión ascendió a diez mil pies y luego se niveló.

meaningEs: ser sincero con alguien, hablar con total franqueza
definitionEn: to tell someone the truth, especially when it is difficult or unpleasant
example1: I need you to level with me about the real state of our company finances.
example1Es: Necesito que seas sincero conmigo sobre el estado real de las finanzas de nuestra empresa.
example2: Instead of hiding the truth, she decided to level with her team members.
example2Es: En lugar de ocultar la verdad, decidió hablar con total franqueza a los miembros de su equipo.

definitionEn: to form a queue or arrange things in a row.
example1: The students lined up outside the classroom door.
example1Es: Los estudiantes hicieron fila fuera de la puerta del salón de clases.
example2: Can you line up the chairs properly?
example2Es: ¿Puedes alinear las sillas correctamente?

meaningEs: ponerse del lado de / apoyar a alguien
definitionEn: to support or agree with a person or group in an argument or conflict.
example1: A good manager should never side with one employee over another.
example1Es: Un buen gerente nunca debe ponerse del lado de un empleado por encima de otro.
example2: She decided to side with her brother during the family dispute.
example2Es: Ella decidió ponerse del lado de su hermano durante la disputa familiar.

meaningEs: hablar más alto, alzar la voz
definitionEn: to speak louder so that people can hear you better.
example1: Could you please speak up? I can't hear you at the back.
example1Es: ¿Podrías hablar más alto, por favor? No te puedo oír al fondo.
example2: She decided to speak up against the unfair policy.
example2Es: Ella decidió alzar la voz en contra de la política injusta.

definitionEn: to state one's opinion firmly and publicly, especially in protest.
example1: It takes courage to speak out against injustice.
example1Es: Se necesita valor para hablar abiertamente en contra de la injusticia.
example2: Several employees spoke out about the poor working conditions.
example2Es: Varios empleados expresaron su opinión en contra de las malas condiciones laborales.

definitionEn: To teach someone the necessary skills to do a specific job well.
example1: They are training up new staff members for the store opening.
example1Es: Están capacitando a nuevos miembros del personal para la apertura de la tienda.
example2: We need to train them up quickly before the busy season.
example2Es: Necesitamos formarlos rápidamente antes de la temporada alta.

definitionEn: To fail to get an advantage or benefit that other people get.
example1: If you don't apply early, you will lose out on a great opportunity.
example1Es: Si no solicitas pronto, te perderás una gran oportunidad.
example2: Many small businesses lost out during the economic downturn.
example2Es: Muchos pequeños negocios salieron perdiendo durante la recesión económica.

definitionEn: To rise from a sitting or lying position.
example1: Everyone stood up when the judge walked in.
example1Es: Todo el mundo se puso de pie cuando entró el juez.
example2: Stand up and stretch your legs for a moment.
example2Es: Levántate y estira las piernas un momento.

definitionEn: To be very noticeable or easily seen among others.
example1: Her bright red coat makes her stand out in the crowd.
example1Es: Su abrigo rojo brillante hace que destaque entre la multitud.
example2: His impressive qualifications made him stand out from other candidates.
example2Es: Sus impresionantes cualificaciones hicieron que destacara sobre los demás candidatos.

definitionEn: To be an abbreviation or symbol for something, or to tolerate a situation.
example1: What do the letters NATO stand for?
example1Es: ¿Qué significan las siglas OTAN?
example2: We will not stand for any bullying in this school.
example2Es: No vamos a tolerar ningún tipo de acoso en esta escuela.

definitionEn: To be ready to act or to support someone loyally.
example1: Emergency services are standing by in case of flooding.
example1Es: Los servicios de emergencia están en espera en caso de inundaciones.
example2: I will always stand by my friends through difficult times.
example2Es: Siempre apoyaré a mis amigos en los momentos difíciles.

definitionEn: to look after someone who is sick, old, or very young, or to like something
example1: He stayed home to care for his elderly mother.
example1Es: Se quedó en casa para cuidar a su madre anciana.
example2: I don't care for spicy food very much.
example2Es: No me gusta mucho la comida picante.

definitionEn: to resolve a problem, or to organize something that is untidy or mixed up
example1: Don't worry, I will sort out the issue with our reservation.
example1Es: No te preocupes, resolveré el problema con nuestra reserva.
example2: We need to sort out the messy files in the office drawer.
example2Es: Necesitamos ordenar los archivos desordenados en el cajón de la oficina.

definitionEn: to break into pieces or experience a mental or emotional collapse
example1: Their marriage began to fall apart after five years.
example1Es: Su matrimonio comenzó a desmoronarse después de cinco años.
example2: After losing his job, he felt like his life was falling apart.
example2Es: Tras perder su empleo, sintió que su vida se venía abajo.

definitionEn: To fail to keep up with a schedule, payments, or peers.
example1: If you miss classes, you will fall behind quickly.
example1Es: Si faltas a clases, te quedarás atrás rápidamente.
example2: The company fell behind its competitors in technology.
example2Es: La empresa se retrasó respecto a sus competidores en tecnología.

meaningEs: enamorarse de / tragar con un engaño
definitionEn: To fall deeply in love with someone, or to be tricked into believing something false.
example1: He fell for her the moment he saw her.
example1Es: Se enamoró de ella en el momento en que la vio.
example2: I can't believe you fell for that obvious scam.
example2Es: No puedo creer que hayas tragado con esa estafa obvia.

definitionEn: To have an argument and stop being friendly with someone.
example1: They fell out over money matters.
example1Es: Se pelearon por cuestiones de dinero.
example2: The two co-founders fell out over intellectual property ownership, leading to a protracted legal dispute.
example2Es: Los dos cofundadores se distanciaron por la titularidad de la propiedad intelectual, lo que condujo a una prolongada disputa legal.

meaningEs: tratar con, lidiar con, ocuparse de
definitionEn: To handle a problem, perform a task, or be about a particular subject.
example1: I need to deal with my emails before I leave.
example1Es: Necesito ocuparme de mis correos electrónicos antes de irme.
example2: The book deals with ancient history.
example2Es: El libro trata sobre historia antigua.

meaningEs: aguar, debilitar, suavizar (un argumento o medida)
definitionEn: To make a liquid weaker by adding water, or to make a statement or plan less severe.
example1: The government had to water down the original proposal to pass the law.
example1Es: El gobierno tuvo que suavizar la propuesta original para aprobar la ley.
example2: Don't water down the juice; it tastes better strong.
example2Es: No le eches agua al jugo; sabe mejor fuerte.

meaningEs: devolver (un producto o artículo por correo o mensajería)
definitionEn: To return something to the person or place it came from, usually by mail.
example1: The shoes were too small, so I had to send them back.
example1Es: Los zapatos eran demasiado pequeños, así que tuve que devolverlos.
example2: He sent the meal back because it was cold.
example2Es: Devolvió la comida porque estaba fría.

definitionEn: to be careful and alert to danger or difficulties.
example1: Watch out for pickpockets in crowded areas.
example1Es: Ten cuidado con los carteristas en las zonas concurridas.
example2: You should watch out when crossing this busy street.
example2Es: Debes tener cuidado al cruzar esta calle tan transitada.

definitionEn: to protect someone or something and make sure they are safe.
example1: The older siblings watch over the younger ones.
example1Es: Los hermanos mayores cuidan de los más pequeños.
example2: An angel watched over him during the storm.
example2Es: Un ángel veló por él durante la tormenta.

definitionEn: to use specific information as the foundation for an argument or creation.
example1: You should base your decisions on facts, not emotions.
example1Es: Debes basar tus decisiones en hechos, no en emociones.
example2: The author based the character on her own sister.
example2Es: La autora basó el personaje en su propia hermana.

definitionEn: to switch off a computer or electronic device completely
example1: Please power down your laptops before leaving the classroom.
example1Es: Por favor, apaguen sus computadoras portátiles antes de salir del aula.
example2: The server automatically powers down at midnight.
example2Es: El servidor se apaga automáticamente a la medianoche.

meaningEs: encender, activar un dispositivo o sistema
definitionEn: to turn on a computer or electronic device and make it ready for use
example1: It takes a few minutes for the main system to power up.
example1Es: Toma unos minutos para que el sistema principal se encienda.
example2: He plugged in the console and powered it up.
example2Es: Conectó la consola y la encendió.

definitionEn: To develop from a child into an adult.
example1: I want to be an astronaut when I grow up.
example1Es: Quiero ser astronauta cuando sea grande.
example2: He grew up in a small town near the mountains.
example2Es: Él creció en un pueblo pequeño cerca de las montañas.

meaningEs: abandonar, declararse en huelga, plantar a alguien
definitionEn: to leave a meeting, performance, or relationship suddenly because you are angry or unhappy
example1: Several employees threatened to walk out if their demands were ignored.
example1Es: Varios empleados amenazaron con irse a la huelga si se ignoraban sus demandas.
example2: He could not believe she would just walk out on her family.
example2Es: No podía creer que ella simplemente fuera a abandonar a su familia.

definitionEn: to explain or show someone how to do something in a careful, step-by-step way
example1: Let me walk you through the new software interface.
example1Es: Permíteme guiarte paso a paso por la nueva interfaz del software.
example2: Can you walk through the procedure one more time?
example2Es: ¿Puedes explicar el procedimiento paso a paso una vez más?

definitionEn: To tell someone to be careful or pay attention to a potential danger.
example1: Mind out! There is a car coming.
example1Es: ¡Cuidado! Viene un coche.
example2: Mind out when handling corrosive chemicals in the research laboratory, and always wear protective eyewear.
example2Es: Ten mucho cuidado al manipular sustancias químicas corrosivas en el laboratorio de investigación, y usa siempre gafas protectoras.

definitionEn: To not go near a place or person.
example1: You should stay away from the construction site; it is dangerous.
example1Es: Deberías mantenerte alejado de la obra en construcción; es peligrosa.
example2: The doctor told him to stay away from greasy foods.
example2Es: El médico le dijo que se mantuviera alejado de las comidas grasosas.

definitionEn: To remain awake and not go to bed at the usual time.
example1: I had to stay up late to finish my history essay.
example1Es: Tuve que quedarme despierto hasta tarde para terminar mi ensayo de historia.
example2: We stayed up all night talking and watching movies.
example2Es: Nos quedamos despiertos toda la noche hablando y viendo películas.

meaningEs: quedarse atrás, quedarse en un lugar cuando los demás se van
definitionEn: To remain in a place after everyone else has left.
example1: She had to stay behind after class to ask the professor a question.
example1Es: Tuvo que quedarse después de clase para hacerle una pregunta al profesor.
example2: The injured hiker had to stay behind while the guide sought help.
example2Es: El excursionista herido tuvo que quedarse atrás mientras el guía buscaba ayuda.

meaningEs: obligar a dimitir, expulsar por la fuerza
definitionEn: To make someone leave a job, position, or place by applying pressure.
example1: The board of directors conspired to force the CEO out of the company.
example1Es: La junta directiva conspiró para obligar al director ejecutivo a dimitir de la empresa.
example2: Rising rents are forcing small local businesses out of the downtown area.
example2Es: El aumento de los alquileres está expulsando a los pequeños negocios locales del centro de la ciudad.

meaningEs: pasar a ver, pasarse por (un lugar)
definitionEn: To visit a place or person briefly while on the way to somewhere else.
example1: I will stop by your office tomorrow morning to drop off the documents.
example1Es: Pasaré por tu oficina mañana por la mañana para dejar los documentos.
example2: Do you want to stop by the bakery on our way home?
example2Es: ¿Quieres que pasemos por la panadería de camino a casa?

meaningEs: hacer escala, pernoctar durante un viaje
definitionEn: To stay at a place for a short time during a long journey, usually when flying.
example1: We are going to stop over in London for two days on our way to Tokyo.
example1Es: Vamos a hacer escala en Londres durante dos días de camino a Tokio.
example2: Many passengers choose to stop over in Dubai when traveling between Europe and Australia.
example2Es: Muchos pasajeros eligen hacer escala en Dubái cuando viajan entre Europa y Australia.

meaningEs: no acostarse, quedarse despierto hasta tarde
definitionEn: To remain awake and not go to bed until late at night.
example1: The children stopped up late to watch the New Year fireworks.
example1Es: Los niños se quedaron despiertos hasta tarde para ver los fuegos artificiales de Año Nuevo.
example2: I had to stop up working to meet the tight deadline.
example2Es: Tuve que quedarme despierto trabajando para cumplir con el ajustado plazo.

definitionEn: To become bright with light or to make something shine.
example1: Her face lit up when she saw the surprise gift.
example1Es: Su rostro se iluminó cuando vio el regalo sorpresa.
example2: City skyscrapers light up the night sky.
example2Es: Los rascacielos de la ciudad iluminan el cielo nocturno.

definitionEn: To divide something among a group of people.
example1: The prize money was shared out equally among the winners.
example1Es: El dinero del premio se repartió equitativamente entre los ganadores.
example2: Please share the food out between everyone.
example2Es: Por favor, reparte la comida entre todos.

definitionEn: To reply rudely to someone in authority.
example1: Children should not answer back to their parents.
example1Es: Los niños no deben replicar a sus padres.
example2: He was punished for answering back.
example2Es: Fue castigado por contestar de mal modo.

definitionEn: To move from a standing position to a sitting position.
example1: Please sit down and make yourself comfortable.
example1Es: Por favor, siéntate y ponte cómodo.
example2: We sat down to discuss the new project.
example2Es: Nos sentamos a debatir sobre el nuevo proyecto.

definitionEn: To choose not to participate in an activity or event.
example1: I am feeling tired, so I will sit out this dance.
example1Es: Me siento cansado, así que no bailaré esta pieza.
example2: Due to a minor injury, he had to sit out the match.
example2Es: Debido a una lesión menor, tuvo que quedarse sin jugar el partido.

definitionEn: To understand or find the answer to a problem by thinking.
example1: I need to figure out how to fix this computer.
example1Es: Necesito averiguar cómo arreglar esta computadora.
example2: Can you figure him out? I find his behavior strange.
example2Es: ¿Puedes comprenderlo? Me parece extraño su comportamiento.

definitionEn: To stop working properly (for a machine) or to lose emotional control.
example1: My car broke down on the way to work this morning.
example1Es: Mi auto se averió de camino al trabajo esta mañana.
example2: She broke down in tears when she heard the bad news.
example2Es: Se echó a llorar cuando oyó la mala noticia.

definitionEn: To end a romantic relationship or to divide into smaller pieces.
example1: They decided to break up after five years together.
example1Es: Decidieron terminar su relación después de cinco años juntos.
example2: The police had to break up the fight.
example2Es: La policía tuvo que disolver la pelea.

definitionEn: To enter a building or car illegally, usually by force.
example1: Someone tried to break into our house last night.
example1Es: Alguien trató de entrar a robar en nuestra casa anoche.
example2: The domestic software firm successfully broke into emerging Latin American and Southeast Asian markets.
example2Es: La empresa nacional de software logró incursionar exitosamente en mercados emergentes de América Latina y el Sudeste Asiático.

definitionEn: To make something clean or tidy, or to explain and solve a misunderstanding or mystery.
example1: We need to clear up this misunderstanding immediately.
example1Es: Necesitamos aclarar este malentendido inmediatamente.
example2: I hope the weather clears up for the weekend.
example2Es: Espero que el tiempo mejore para el fin de semana.

definitionEn: To empty a place of unwanted objects or leave a place quickly.
example1: It is time to clear out the garage and throw away old junk.
example1Es: Es hora de vaciar el garaje y tirar la vieja chatarra.
example2: The police told the crowd to clear out.
example2Es: La policía le dijo a la multitud que se fuera.

meaningEs: completar, llenar hasta el borde, rematar
definitionEn: To fill something completely, or finish something in a special way.
example1: Let me top off your coffee.
example1Es: Déjame llenarte el café.
example2: We topped off the vacation with a great dinner.
example2Es: Rematamos las vacaciones con una gran cena.

definitionEn: To successfully persuade someone to agree with you or support you.
example1: His brilliant speech helped win over the skeptical audience.
example1Es: Su brillante discurso ayudó a convencer al público escéptico.
example2: It is hard to win them over once they have made up their minds.
example2Es: Es difícil convencerlos una vez que han tomado una decisión.

definitionEn: To show someone that you are interested in them and want to help them or offer support.
example1: If you need any guidance, please reach out to me.
example1Es: Si necesitas orientación, por favor comunícate conmigo.
example2: Charities often reach out to vulnerable communities.
example2Es: Las organizaciones benéficas a menudo contactan a comunidades vulnerables.

definitionEn: to write something down on paper so that you do not forget it
example1: Please note down the address before you lose it.
example1Es: Por favor, apunta la dirección antes de que la pierdas.
example2: He noted down all the key points from the meeting.
example2Es: Anotó todos los puntos clave de la reunión.

definitionEn: To leave in a vehicle or make someone/something go away by being unpleasant.
example1: He got into his car and drove away.
example1Es: Se subió a su coche y se alejó conduciendo.
example2: Poor customer service can drive away loyal clients.
example2Es: Un mal servicio al cliente puede alejar a los clientes leales.

definitionEn: To approach in a vehicle or cause prices/costs to increase rapidly.
example1: A red sports car drove up to the front entrance.
example1Es: Un coche deportivo rojo se acercó a la entrada principal.
example2: Bad weather can drive up the price of fresh vegetables.
example2Es: El mal tiempo puede hacer subir el precio de las verduras frescas.

definitionEn: To write something in its final form using a computer, based on notes or a rough draft.
example1: I need to type up my notes from the meeting.
example1Es: Necesito pasar a limpio mis notas de la reunión.
example2: Can you type it up by tomorrow?
example2Es: ¿Puedes pasarlo a limpio para mañana?

meaningEs: sonsacar, sondear la opinión de alguien
definitionEn: To try to find out what someone thinks about something by talking to them.
example1: We need to sound out the manager before making a final decision.
example1Es: Necesitamos sondear al gerente antes de tomar una decisión final.
example2: She sounded him out about the new project.
example2Es: Ella le sondeó sobre el nuevo proyecto.

definitionEn: To stay in a place until someone or something arrives or happens.
example1: I am waiting for the bus.
example1Es: Estoy esperando el autobús.
example2: Can you wait for me a moment?
example2Es: ¿Puedes esperarme un momento?

definitionEn: To stay awake and not go to bed because you are expecting someone to arrive.
example1: Don't wait up for me tonight; I will be very late.
example1Es: No me esperen despiertos esta noche; llegaré muy tarde.
example2: She waited up until midnight to make sure her son got home safely.
example2Es: Ella se quedó despierta hasta la medianoche para asegurarse de que su hijo llegara sano y salvo a casa.

definitionEn: To join with another person or group in order to do something together.
example1: They decided to team up for the final project.
example1Es: Decidieron unirse para el proyecto final.
example2: Local businesses teamed up to sponsor the charity event.
example2Es: Los negocios locales se unieron para patrocinar el evento benéfico.

definitionEn: to make sense or seem reasonable.
example1: His story simply doesn't add up.
example1Es: Su historia simplemente no tiene sentido.
example2: The receipts don't add up correctly.
example2Es: Los recibos no suman correctamente.

definitionEn: to state that something is not possible or is not suitable.
example1: Police have not ruled out foul play in the investigation.
example1Es: La policía no ha descartado el juego sucio en la investigación.
example2: We cannot rule out the possibility of rain tomorrow.
example2Es: No podemos descartar la posibilidad de lluvia mañana.

definitionEn: a polite expression for dying.
example1: His grandfather passed away peacefully last night.
example1Es: Su abuelo falleció pacíficamente anoche.
example2: She was deeply saddened when her pet passed away.
example2Es: Se entristeció profundamente cuando su mascota falleció.

definitionEn: to lose consciousness.
example1: It was so hot in the room that she almost passed out.
example1Es: Hacía tanto calor en la habitación que casi se desmaya.
example2: He felt dizzy and passed out during the marathon.
example2Es: Se sintió mareado y se desmayó durante el maratón.

definitionEn: To sell all of the supply of something so that none is left.
example1: The concert tickets sold out within ten minutes.
example1Es: Las entradas para el concierto se agotaron en diez minutos.
example2: They sold out all their merchandise before the festival ended.
example2Es: Vendieron toda su mercancía antes de que terminara el festival.

definitionEn: To try to stop people from knowing about a mistake, crime, or unpleasant fact.
example1: They tried to cover up the scandal.
example1Es: Intentaron encubrir el escándalo.
example2: Don't try to cover it up; tell the truth.
example2Es: No intentes ocultarlo; di la verdad.

meaningEs: explicar, dar razón de / representar un porcentaje
definitionEn: To explain the cause of something, or to be a particular part or amount of something.
example1: Bad weather accounts for the delay in our flight.
example1Es: El mal tiempo explica la demora en nuestro vuelo.
example2: Electric cars account for a growing percentage of total sales.
example2Es: Los autos eléctricos representan un porcentaje creciente de las ventas totales.

definitionEn: To compare prices and quality from different shops before deciding what to buy.
example1: It is smart to shop around before buying a new computer.
example1Es: Es inteligente comparar precios antes de comprar una computadora nueva.
example2: She shopped around for weeks to find the best car insurance.
example2Es: Ella comparó precios durante semanas para encontrar el mejor seguro de auto.

definitionEn: To continue doing an activity or task without stopping.
example1: Please carry on with your work while I am out.
example1Es: Por favor, continúa con tu trabajo mientras estoy fuera.
example2: Despite the rain, they decided to carry on walking.
example2Es: A pesar de la lluvia, decidieron seguir caminando.

definitionEn: To perform or complete a task, plan, or experiment.
example1: The scientists will carry out the tests tomorrow morning.
example1Es: Los científicos realizarán las pruebas mañana por la mañana.
example2: The company failed to carry out the agreed repairs.
example2Es: La empresa no llevó a cabo las reparaciones acordadas.

definitionEn: to become extinct or disappear completely over time
example1: Dinosaurs died out millions of years ago.
example1Es: Los dinosaurios se extinguieron hace millones de años.
example2: Old customs tend to die out in modern society.
example2Es: Las viejas costumbres tienden a desaparecer en la sociedad moderna.

definitionEn: to become less loud, strong, or active
example1: We waited for the storm to die down before leaving.
example1Es: Esperamos a que la tormenta amainara antes de salir.
example2: The applause eventually died down after a few minutes.
example2Es: Los aplausos finalmente disminuyeron después de unos minutos.

definitionEn: to support the truth of something or confirm a statement
example1: The evidence bears out his version of events.
example1Es: Las pruebas confirman su versión de los hechos.
example2: Subsequent studies will likely bear out these preliminary findings.
example2Es: Es probable que estudios posteriores corroboren estos hallazgos preliminares.

meaningEs: mantenerse firme, resistir ante la adversidad
definitionEn: to remain as cheerful or firm as possible in a difficult situation
example1: She is bearing up remarkably well under the circumstances.
example1Es: Ella se está manteniendo firme notablemente bien dadas las circunstancias.
example2: He managed to bear up despite receiving the tragic news.
example2Es: Se las arregló para resistir a pesar de recibir la trágica noticia.

definitionEn: to do less of something or use less of something, or to fell a tree
example1: The doctor told him to cut down on sugar.
example1Es: El médico le dijo que redujera el consumo de azúcar.
example2: They had to cut down the old oak tree because it was diseased.
example2Es: Tuvieron que talar el viejo roble porque estaba enfermo.

definitionEn: to disconnect, interrupt, or isolate someone or something
example1: The heavy snowstorm cut off electricity to the village.
example1Es: La fuerte tormenta de nieve cortó la electricidad del pueblo.
example2: He was cut off in the middle of his sentence during the phone call.
example2Es: Le interrumpieron a mitad de su frase durante la llamada telefónica.

definitionEn: to stop eating or doing something, or to remove a piece with scissors
example1: I decided to cut out all processed foods from my diet.
example1Es: Decidí eliminar todos los alimentos procesados de mi dieta.
example2: She cut out pictures from the magazine for her collage.
example2Es: Recortó imágenes de la revista para su collage.

definitionEn: To fight against a leader or government; to rebel.
example1: The citizens decided to rise up against the oppressive regime.
example1Es: Los ciudadanos decidieron rebelarse contra el régimen opresivo.
example2: Oppressed citizens across the region rose up against the authoritarian regime to demand democratic elections.
example2Es: Ciudadanos oprimidos de toda la región se sublevaron contra el régimen autoritario para exigir elecciones democráticas.

definitionEn: To take part in an activity with other people who are already doing it.
example1: Everyone started singing, and I decided to join in.
example1Es: Todos empezaron a cantar y decidí unirme.
example2: Don't be shy; please join in the game.
example2Es: No seas tímido; por favor, participa en el juego.

definitionEn: To become a member of the armed forces.
example1: He decided to join up and serve in the army after finishing school.
example1Es: Decidió alistarse y servir en el ejército después de terminar la escuela.
example2: Several regional transit authorities joined up to launch a unified electronic ticketing system.
example2Es: Varias autoridades regionales de transporte se unieron para poner en marcha un sistema unificado de billetes electrónicos.

meaningEs: comer fuera de casa (en un restaurante)
definitionEn: to have a meal in a restaurant rather than at home
example1: We usually eat out on Friday nights.
example1Es: Solemos comer fuera los viernes por la noche.
example2: Would you prefer to cook at home or eat out tonight?
example2Es: ¿Preferirías cocinar en casa o comer fuera esta noche?

definitionEn: to eat all of the food that you have been given
example1: Eat up your vegetables, or you won't get any dessert.
example1Es: Termínate las verduras o no obtendrás postre.
example2: She told the children to eat everything up quickly.
example2Es: Ella les dijo a los niños que se comieran todo rápidamente.

definitionEn: to officially leave a position or job, especially a high-ranking one
example1: The CEO decided to step down after ten years at the company.
example1Es: El director ejecutivo decidió dimitir tras diez años en la empresa.
example2: Pressure from the board forced the director to step down.
example2Es: La presión de la junta directiva obligó al director a dimitir.

meaningEs: intensificar, aumentar, dar un paso al frente
definitionEn: to increase the amount, speed, or intensity of something, or to take action when needed
example1: The company needs to step up its production to meet customer demand.
example1Es: La empresa necesita intensificar su producción para satisfacer la demanda de los clientes.
example2: When the crisis hit, the employees stepped up to help.
example2Es: Cuando llegó la crisis, los empleados dieron un paso al frente para ayudar.

definitionEn: to move so that someone else can pass or take your place
example1: He stepped aside to let the elderly woman pass through the doorway.
example1Es: Se hizo a un lado para dejar pasar a la anciana por la puerta.
example2: The aging chairman agreed to step aside and allow a younger executive to steer the corporation's digital transition.
example2Es: El veterano presidente aceptó dar un paso al costado y permitir que un ejecutivo más joven dirigiera la transición digital de la corporación.

definitionEn: to call someone on the telephone
example1: She phoned up her mother to tell her the good news.
example1Es: Llamó a su madre por teléfono para contarle la buena noticia.
example2: I need to phone him up before the office closes.
example2Es: Necesito llamarle por teléfono antes de que cierre la oficina.

meaningEs: llamar para reportarse o dar información
definitionEn: to telephone a place of work to report information, an absence, or news
example1: He had to phone in sick because he caught a bad flu.
example1Es: Tuvo que llamar para avisar que estaba enfermo porque cogió una fuerte gripe.
example2: Employees who are unable to report to the office due to severe illness are required to phone in by eight in the morning.
example2Es: Los empleados que no puedan presentarse en la oficina debido a una enfermedad grave deben llamar para avisar antes de las ocho de la mañana.

meaningEs: prolongar, alargar o hacer que alguien se vuelva más sociable y comunicativo
definitionEn: To make something last longer than usual, or to help someone feel less shy.
example1: Do not draw out the meeting any longer than necessary.
example1Es: No alargues la reunión más tiempo del necesario.
example2: The teacher tried to draw out the quiet student during the discussion.
example2Es: El profesor intentó hacer que el alumno callado participara más durante la discusión.

meaningEs: redactar un documento o detenerse (un vehículo)
definitionEn: To prepare a legal document or plan, or for a vehicle to come to a stop.
example1: The lawyer will draw up a formal contract tomorrow.
example1Es: El abogado redactará un contrato formal mañana.
example2: A black car drew up outside the office.
example2Es: Un coche negro se detuvo frente a la oficina.

definitionEn: To have origins that go back to a particular time in the past.
example1: This old castle dates back to the fourteenth century.
example1Es: Este viejo castillo se remonta al siglo XIV.
example2: Their friendship dates back to their college days.
example2Es: Su amistad data de sus días de universidad.

meaningEs: terminar en un lugar o situación imprevista
definitionEn: To eventually arrive in a particular place or situation, often unexpectedly.
example1: If you don't study hard, you might land up working a job you hate.
example1Es: Si no estudias duro, podrías terminar trabajando en un empleo que odias.
example2: We missed our train and landed up taking a taxi.
example2Es: Perdimos nuestro tren y acabamos tomando un taxi.
